title.full: ASEAN Green Future Project Phase 2.2 Report, Optimization of Laos's Power Generation Sector

publisher.full: Sustainable Development Solutions Network and ClimateWorks Centre

description: Cost-optimized pathway under current policies with coal and hydropower expansion.

coreDrivers.policies: Hydro capacity additions in 2030 aligned with NDCs, then additional additions are included based on ressource potential assessment and least cost optimization.
coreDrivers.technologyCosts: Least-cost optimization determines dispatch and generation mix.
coreDrivers.macroeconomicDrivers: SSP2 GDP, medium population growth extracted from World Bank and sectoral value-added trends from country target drive electricity demand.
coreDrivers.otherDrivers: Hydropower resource potential is the main constraint for end-year capacity mix.

dependencies.dependency_description: Hydro capacity additions in 2030 aligned with NDCs, then additional additions are included based on ressource potential assessment.
The regulatory framework is represented mainly through national plans and standards, not detailed market design or permitting.

OEP deals with economics explicitly through least-cost optimization: with the same installed capacity as EP, generation shifts heavily toward hydropower and coal while wind, solar, and biomass generation fall to zero in 2050.

EP imposes demand-side adoption assumptions exogenously, including passenger EV penetration of 30% in 2030 and 60% in 2050 and lower electric-truck uptake. These assumptions increase power demand but are not framed as a power-sector bottleneck.

OEP expands significantly hydro capacities. Hydropower facilities are typically situated in isolated regions and require integration with the national system to distribute energy nationwide. However, OEP does not quantify transmission expansion or model grid integration as a constraint. Hydro power plant are able to generate twice more electricity than in EP. This implies greater utilization of the hydro system, but no corresponding pathway-specific transmission/logistics expansion is modelled.

Hydropower maxiumum potential ressources is reached by 2050 and is the limit to hydro expansion in Lao. Even if the same amount of hydropower capacity is build out by 2050, those capacities generate twice more power than in Existing Policies pathway. These shifts are due to an optimizing the use of existing resources with least cost,.

Seasonal water availability affects hydropower adequacy in the dry season. Laos power grid is already dependant on Thailand during that period. OEP does not introduce a future change in hydrology or an environmental constraint on hydro deployment. OEP therefore proceeds using the stated hydro potential without modelling future ecosystem/climate impacts.
The electrical system requires substantial human resources for its operation. This is not measured in this analysis.
